1245-night-and-day.title: Night And Day
1245-night-and-day.creator: Virginia Woolf
1245-night-and-day.description: A book by Virginia Woolf. It suddenly came into Katharine’s mind that if some one opened the door at this moment he would think that they were enjoying themselves; he would think, “What an extremely nice house to come into!” and instinctively she laughed, and said something to increase the noise, for the credit of the house presumably, since she herself had not been feeling exhilarated.

63028-reinstern.title: Reinstern
63028-reinstern.creator: Unknown
63028-reinstern.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. It seemed rather a mixture of many delicious odors. Fertile fields and wooded hills stretched away before us; men, women and children in ideal peasant costumes moved gaily about, chatting together, singing, dancing over the velvety sod, or leaping and swinging from the supple boughs while pelting each other with blossoms or gathering the luscious fruit which was everywhere temptingly abundant.

74964-the-cambridge-natural-history-vol-.title: The Cambridge Natural History Vol 09 Of 10
74964-the-cambridge-natural-history-vol-.creator: Unknown
74964-the-cambridge-natural-history-vol-.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. Prefixed to each group is a brief summary of the Structure and Habits; a few further particulars of the same nature being subsequently added where necessary, with a statement of the main Fossil forms as yet recorded.

arxiv-2109-12315.title: Entanglement Emerges from Dissipation-Structured Quantum Self-Organization
arxiv-2109-12315.creator: Zhi-Bo Yang, Yi-Pu Wang, Jie Li, C.-M. Hu, J. Q. You
arxiv-2109-12315.description: Abstract Entanglement is a holistic property of multipartite quantum systems, which is accompanied by the establishment of nonclassical correlations between subsystems. Most entanglement mechanisms can be described by a coherent interaction Hamiltonian, and entanglement develops over time. In other words, the generation of entanglement has a time arrow. Dissipative structure theory directs the evolving time arrow of a non-equilibrium system.

arxiv-2404-05588.title: Cohomology ring of non-compact abelian arrangements
arxiv-2404-05588.creator: Evienia Bazzocchi, Roberto Pagaria, Maddalena Pismataro
arxiv-2404-05588.description: Abstract . We give a Orlik-Solomon type presentation for the cohomology ring of arrangements in a non-compact abelian Lie group. The new insight consists in comparing arrangements in different abelian groups. Our work is based on the Varchenko-Gel’fand ring for real hyperplane arrangements and from that we deduce the cohomology rings of all other abelian arrangements.

arxiv-2502-14501.title: Towards a Perspectivist Turn in Argument Quality Assessment
arxiv-2502-14501.creator: Julia Romberg, Maximilian Maurer, Henning Wachsmuth, Gabriella Lapesa
arxiv-2502-14501.description: Abstract The assessment of argument quality depends on well-established logical, rhetorical, and dialectical properties that are unavoidably subjective: multiple valid assessments may exist, there is no unequivocal ground truth. This aligns with recent paths in machine learning, which embrace the co-existence of different perspectives. However, this potential remains largely unexplored in NLP research on argument quality.

arxiv-2504-03345.title: Time Varying Resonators in Acoustic Waveguides: A Transfer Matrix Formalism for Space-time Modulated Metamaterials
arxiv-2504-03345.creator: D. Cidlinský 1,2, G. J. Chaplain 2 and S. A. R. Horsley 2
arxiv-2504-03345.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by D. Cidlinský 1,2, G. J. Chaplain 2 and S. A. R. Horsley 2. The transfer matrix method remains a simple yet powerful tool for modeling acoustic systems, particularly in a closed waveguide geometry. Here we present a generalisation of this method based on the theory of mode matching, that incorporates the effect of ultra–fast temporal variations in the geometry, applying it to a system of side-branching resonant cavities (quarter wavelength resonators) fixed to an acoustic waveguide, modulated through alteration of the cavity length.

arxiv-2508-09466.title: Event-driven Robust Fitting on Neuromorphic Hardware
arxiv-2508-09466.creator: Tam Ngoc-Bang Nguyen, Anh-Dzung Doan, Zhipeng Cai, Tat-Jun Chin
arxiv-2508-09466.description: Abstract Robust fitting of geometric models is a fundamental task in many computer vision pipelines. Numerous innovations have been produced on the topic, from improving the efficiency and accuracy of random sampling heuristics to generating novel theoretical insights that underpin new approaches with mathematical guarantees. However, one aspect of robust fitting that has received little attention is energy efficiency.

plos-pone-0010469.title: In Mice, Tuberculosis Progression Is Associated with Intensive Inflammatory Response and the Accumulation of Gr-1 dim Cells in the Lungs
plos-pone-0010469.creator: Irina V. Lyadova, Evgeny N. Tsiganov, Marina A. Kapina et al.
plos-pone-0010469.description: PLOS ONE research article. Infection with Mycobacterium tuberculosis ( Mtb ) results in different clinical outcomes ranging from asymptomatic containment to rapidly progressing tuberculosis (TB). The mechanisms controlling TB progression in immunologically-competent hosts remain unclear. To address these m

pmc-10610892.title: An RNA-Scaffold Protein Subunit Vaccine for Nasal Immunization
pmc-10610892.creator: Joy-Yan Lam, Wan-Man Wong, Chun-Kit Yuen, Yau-Yee Ng, Chun-Hin San, Kwok-Yung Yuen, Kin-Hang Kok
pmc-10610892.description: Developing recombinant proteins as nasal vaccines for inducing systemic and mucosal immunity against respiratory viruses is promising. However, additional adjuvants are required to overcome the low immunogenicity of protein antigens. Here, a self-adjuvanted protein-RNA ribonucleoprotein vaccine was developed and found to be an effective nasal vaccine in mice and the SARS-CoV-2 infection model.

pmc-10673370.title: Genetic Variants in Matrix Metalloproteinases MMP3 (rs3025058) and MMP9 (rs3918242) Associated with Colonic Diverticulosis
pmc-10673370.creator: Piotr Nehring, Grażyna Gromadzka, Miłosz Jastrzębski, Adam Przybyłkowski, Cristian George Ţieranu, Adrian Saftoiu
pmc-10673370.description: Background and Objectives: Diverticulosis affects a significant portion of the elderly population, with age and lifestyle being established risk factors. Additionally, genetic predisposition is gaining recognition as a contributing factor. This pilot study sought to explore the frequency of genetic variants in matrix metalloproteinases (MMPs) 3, 9, and 12 in a population of colonic diverticulosis patients.

pmc-11301841.title: Choroidal vascular changes in early-stage myopic maculopathy from deep learning choroidal analysis: a hospital-based SS-OCT study
pmc-11301841.creator: Yan Li, Haoer Li, Xue Rui, Yuan Wang, Shenju Zhu, Mengge Huang, Jianqiang Liang, Yangfeifei Zhu, Jiajia Shi, Le Yu, Shenghai Huang, Chun Yang, Mengmeng Dong, Hebei Gao, Meixiao Shen, Hao Wu, Xiangtian Zhou
pmc-11301841.description: BackgroundThe objective of this study is to illustrate the changes in the choroidal vasculature in individuals with diffuse chorioretinal atrophy (DCA, early-stage myopic maculopathy) and investigate the association between them.MethodsThis study included 1418 highly myopic eyes from 720 participants aged 18 − 60 years from the Wenzhou High Myopia Cohort Study. These participants underwent comprehensive ophthalmic assessments.

pmc-11347313.title: Transcription factor ZEB1 coordinating with NuRD complex to promote oncogenesis through glycolysis in colorectal cancer
pmc-11347313.creator: Tianyang Gao, Xinhui Hao, Jingyao Zhang, Miaomiao Huo, Ting Hu, Tianyu Ma, Hefen Yu, Xu Teng, Yong Wang, Yunkai Yang, Wei Huang, Yan Wang
pmc-11347313.description: BackgroundColorectal cancer (CRC) is an aggressive primary intestinal malignancy with the third-highest incidence and second-highest mortality among all cancer types worldwide. Transcription factors (TFs) regulate cell development and differentiation owing to their ability to recognize specific DNA sequences upstream of genes. Numerous studies have demonstrated a strong correlation between TFs, the etiology of tumors, and therapeutic approaches.

pmc-11358292.title: A bright burst from FRB 20200120E in a globular cluster of the nearby galaxy M81
pmc-11358292.creator: S. B. Zhang, J. S. Wang, X. Yang, Y. Li, J. J. Geng, Z. F. Tang, C. M. Chang, J. T. Luo, X. C. Wang, X. F. Wu, Z. G. Dai, B. Zhang
pmc-11358292.description: Fast radio bursts (FRBs) are immensely energetic millisecond-duration radio pulses. Observations indicate that nearby FRBs can be produced by old stellar populations, as suggested by the localization of the repeating source FRB 20200120E in a globular cluster of M81. Nevertheless, the burst energies of FRB 20200120E are significantly smaller than those of other cosmological FRBs.

pmc-11428131.title: Stability and Dynamics of Zeolite-Confined Gold Nanoclusters
pmc-11428131.creator: Siddharth Sonti, Chenghan Sun, Zekun Chen, Robert Michael Kowalski, Joseph S Kowalski, Davide Donadio, Surl-Hee Ahn, Ambarish R Kulkarni
pmc-11428131.description: Nanoengineered metal@zeolite materials have recently emerged as a promising class of catalysts for several industrially relevant reactions. These materials, which consist of small transition metal nanoclusters confined within three-dimensional zeolite pores, are interesting because they show higher stability and better sintering resistance under reaction conditions.

pmc-11431942.title: Advancements in the Diagnosis and Treatment of Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy: A Comprehensive Review
pmc-11431942.creator: Randeep Gill, Arsalan Siddiqui, Brianna Yee, Michael V. DiCaro, Nazanin Houshmand, Tahir Tak
pmc-11431942.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) is characterized by excessive growth of myocardial tissue, most commonly due to genetic mutations in sarcomere proteins. This can lead to complications such as heart failure, mitral regurgitation, syncope, arrhythmias, sudden cardiac death, and myocardial ischemia. While we have come a long way in our understanding of the pathophysiology, genetics, and epidemiology of HCM, the past 10 years have seen significant advancements in diagnosis and treatment.

pmc-11439340.title: Busin Glide-Assisted Pull-Through Insertion of Artificial Corneal Endothelium (EndoArt)
pmc-11439340.creator: Akira Kobayashi, Takahiko Hayashi, Ami Igarashi, Toshiki Shimizu, Hideaki Yokogawa, Kentaro Yuda, Björn Bachmann, Satoru Yamagami, Kazuhisa Sugiyama
pmc-11439340.description: BackgroundCurrently, the push-in technique through the corneal tunnel using a blunt-tip spatula is used to insert an artificial corneal endothelium (EndoArt) into the anterior chamber (AC). The device is useful for patients with bullous keratopathy; however, it may be difficult to manipulate the very thin implant through hazy cornea.

pmc-12439457.title: Circular RNAs: Fundamental mechanisms in tumor metastasis and detection strategies (Review)
pmc-12439457.creator: Xiangjun Dong, Yinwei Che, Yuzhuo Jiao, Hao Dong, Qingchao Ren, Huashan Sun, Tao Zhao
pmc-12439457.description: As a class of endogenous non-coding RNAs, circular RNAs (circRNAs) are produced by an event known as back-splicing. Although circRNAs were initially considered to be the product of abnormal splicing events, increasing evidence has shown their vital role in the development of various diseases, especially malignant tumors.

pmc-12452911.title: From molecular damage and viscoelasticity to interfacial fracture in soft polymer networks: Insights from mechanochemistry
pmc-12452911.creator: Anthony Arrowood, Jackson Frazier, Matteo Ciccotti, Gabriel E. Sanoja
pmc-12452911.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). SignificanceUnraveling the interplay between time-dependent material properties and the dynamic process of crack propagation is essential for developing a fundamental understanding of fracture in soft polymer networks. Such knowledge is critical for predicting and preventing catastrophic failures across engineering and biological applications and for enabling the rational design of advanced materials with sufficient toughness and predictable service lifetime under diverse loading and environmental conditions.

pmc-12621256.title: Success and Limitations of Current Force Fields for the Description of RNA–Ligand Complexes
pmc-12621256.creator: Paula Fernández Migens, Israel Serrano-Chacón, Modesto Orozco, Federica Battistini
pmc-12621256.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). We present a systematic assessment of the last generation of RNA force fields to reproduce the structures and dynamics of ligand–RNA complexes. Our comprehensive analysis helped not only to define the more reliable force field to represent complex structures but also suggests details that can be improved and provide a critical analysis of the quality of experimental structures in complex systems that are expected to be very flexible and environment dependent.

pmc-13098497.title: SCAR-Net-assisted ultrasound diagnosis of postoperative scars and recurrent lesions in breast cancer
pmc-13098497.creator: Na Feng, Shanshan Zhao, Zhikai Lei, Dan Yi, Jincao Yao, Xiao Zhang, Xiangyang Li, Weijie Zou, Jian Zhang, Liyu Chen, Chen Yang, Dong Xu, Yong Wu
pmc-13098497.description: SummaryPostoperative differentiation between scar tissue and recurrent lesions in patients with breast cancer presents a significant diagnostic challenge. This study introduces SCAR-Net, a deep learning model specifically designed for ultrasound-based discrimination between these similar-appearing tissues. Using 34,376 ultrasound images from 5,710 patients across four hospitals, we developed a model incorporating scar-recurrence feature enhancer and boundary-sensitive attention network modules.

pmc-13135518.title: The Association Between Shared Decision-Making and Child Health in the General Pediatric Population
pmc-13135518.creator: Alyssa Cohen, Kelly N. Michelson, Michelle L. Macy, Nia Heard-Garris, Kristin Kan
pmc-13135518.description: ObjectiveShared decision-making (SDM) is a decision-making approach that aims to enhance collaboration between patients and providers. SDM is associated with improved health outcomes and decreased healthcare expenditure among children with special health care needs. However, much remains unknown about the role of SDM in the broader general pediatric population.

pmc-13374991.title: Prevalence of Oral Soft Tissue Lesions and Their Associations with Oral Hygiene Practices, Addictive Habits, and CD4 Counts Among Lesbian, Gay, Bisexual, Transgender, and Queer Individuals Living with Human Immunodeficiency Virus
pmc-13374991.creator: Shrikanth Muralidharan, Pramila Mallaiah, Deepak Bangera, Arunkumar Acharya, Judy Annie Koshy, Monali Nikalje
pmc-13374991.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Objectives:Oral manifestations often reflect underlying immune suppression and disease progression. These lesions can profoundly affect the quality of life, leading to pain, difficulty in eating, and social stigma. In the lesbian, gay, bisexual, transgender, and queer (LGBTQ) population living with human immunodeficiency virus (HIV), additional sociobehavioral factors, such as discrimination, mental health challenges, and barriers to healthcare access, may exacerbate oral health issues.Material and Methods:This cross-sectional study aimed to evaluate the prevalence of oral soft tissue lesions and their associations with oral

pmc-13406968.title: The Value of the Albumin–Myosteatosis Gauge in Predicting the Postoperative Outcomes of Non-Metastatic Gastric Cancer
pmc-13406968.creator: Huihui Zhang, Yunshi Huang, Jiacheng Jiang, Yuchen Wang, Xiangyang Xue, Xinxin Yang
pmc-13406968.description: Simple SummaryCurrent reports indicate that 60–80% of patients with gastric cancer (GC) develop cachexia, which ultimately leads to elevated cancer-specific mortality and increased treatment-related toxicity. In the context of precachexia, a close correlation has been observed between systemic inflammation and muscle wasting.

pmc-13421479.title: Semantic embedding of variant effect annotations enables rapid and accurate pathogenicity prediction with VUS.Life
pmc-13421479.creator: Jiawei Wu, Marissa Stutzman, Michael Muriello, Joy Lincoln, Donald G. Basel, Xiaowu Gai
pmc-13421479.description: Interpreting the pathogenicity of genetic variants remains a critical bottleneck in genomic medicine. Millions of variants of uncertain significance (VUS) hinder the clinical application of genetic findings. Traditional computational approaches often rely on hand-engineered features and fail to capture the complexity of multidimensional genomic annotations fully. We developed VUS.

pmc-13477353.title: Associations of Physical Activity With Mortality Across Cardiovascular–Kidney–Metabolic Syndrome Stages: Evidence From NHANES 1999 to 2018
pmc-13477353.creator: Yangjie Xiao, Cheng Cheng, Le Zhang, Jinling Hu, Lei Wang, Cong Shang, Song Gao, Bing Ma, Hao Sun, Jing Zhang
pmc-13477353.description: BackgroundCardiovascular–kidney–metabolic (CKM) syndrome integrates cardiovascular, renal, and metabolic dysfunction and is associated with high mortality. Stage‐stratified evidence linking physical activity (PA) to mortality remains limited.MethodsWe analyzed 19 930 adults with CKM stages 0 to 4 from the NHANES (National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey, 1999–2018), with mortality follow‐up through 2019.

pmc-13661741.title: Comparison of traditional and new treatments for fibrous dysplasia: a systematic review and meta-analysis
pmc-13661741.creator: Lucie Levaillant, Guillaume Mabilleau, Adèle Malagié, Sixtine Donat, Régis Coutant, Patrice Rodien, Claire Briet
pmc-13661741.description: IntroductionFibrous dysplasia, alone or associated with McCune-Albright syndrome, is a rare bone disorder that can cause pain, deformity, fractures, and thus affect quality of life. Various treatments have been tried, starting with bisphosphonate administration, and now targeted therapies are being developed.
